transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: good evening thank you for calling S-Net technical support my name is kieran who am i speaking with tonight

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: hi kieran it's padraig here i'm ringing up because i'm getting dreadful packet loss and massive 180 millisecond lag spikes on my gaming console every evening

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: hey padraig i'm really sorry you're getting hit with 180 millisecond lag spikes and packet loss like that i know how frustrating rubber-banding is when you're trying to play online

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: tell me about it mate i've been kicked out of three ranked matches in a row tonight and my teammates are raging at me

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: so just to paraphrase what you're seeing even though your broadband line is up your gaming console is suffering severe intermittent packet loss and jitter spikes up to 180 milliseconds during online play

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: spot on kieran when i run a normal download test it gets like 75 megabits but in game the packet loss graph lights up red every twenty seconds

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: i'm going to take full ownership of tracking down where those dropped packets are coming from padraig before i pull up your line diagnostics can you confirm your home address and four digit security PIN

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: yeah no problem it's 112 saint patrick's road coventry CV1 2LP and the security PIN is 6104

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: cheers padraig and could you also confirm the answer to your security question which is your favourite football team

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: that's celtic

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: brilliant that's all verified on my side padraig i can see your S-Net Fibre 500 line and your Hub 4 router connected here at 112 saint patrick's road

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: nice one so can you see if the fibre line outside is dropping packets

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: let's test both the external fibre link and your internal setup first let me ask a few probing questions about how your console is connected to the Hub 4

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: sure go ahead

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: what console are you playing on padraig and have you got an ethernet cable plugged straight into the back of the S-Net Hub 4 or is it going through something else

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: i'm on a PlayStation 5 in the back bedroom and i've got an ethernet cable plugged into the PS5 so it shows as a wired LAN connection

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: aha and where does the other end of that ethernet cable in the back bedroom plug into does it run all the way through the walls to the hallway router

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: no it plugs into one of those white TP-Link AV600 powerline homeplug adapters in the wall socket and the matching homeplug is by the router

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: interesting how old are those TP-Link AV600 powerline adapters and are either of them plugged into a multi-way extension lead or surge strip

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: i've had them about five years from my old house and yeah the one near the router is plugged into a four way extension strip on the kitchen partition wall

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: and what else is plugged into that kitchen extension strip or running on the kitchen sockets in the evening when you get the 180 millisecond spikes

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: uh the microwave is on that strip and the condenser tumble dryer and washing machine are right next to it on the same kitchen wall

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: padraig i think we have just uncovered the smoking gun right there when did you put the tumble dryer on tonight

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: no way my partner switched the tumble dryer on at half seven right before we queued up for ranked matches

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: let me prove it scientifically for you first please bear with me for just over a minute while i run a 1000-packet high-frequency ping test directly from our core exchange to your Hub 4 WAN port

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: thanks so much for waiting padraig the 1000-packet WAN ping test to your Hub 4 just finished and the external fibre line had zero percent packet loss

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: zero percent loss on the fibre line what was the ping time to the router

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: average latency was 5.8 milliseconds with only 0.4 milliseconds of jitter across all one thousand packets so your Fibre 500 line to the street cabinet is rock solid

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: wow 6 milliseconds so the lag spikes are 100 percent coming from those TP-Link powerline plugs then

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: 100 percent mate old AV600 homeplugs send data over your home's copper electrical wiring and whenever a tumble dryer motor or compressor cycles it floods the power circuit with high-frequency electrical noise

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: and plugging the adapter into a four-way extension strip makes it even worse doesn't it

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: spot on extension leads filter out the high frequency carrier signal and when the dryer drum spins the homeplug has to retransmit corrupted frames which causes those 180ms jitter spikes

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: that makes total sense because on saturday afternoon when nobody was doing laundry my ping was completely fine

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: how far is the back bedroom from the hallway Hub 4 padraig is it on the same floor or upstairs

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: it's a ground floor flat so the back bedroom is literally about six metres down the hallway with just one plasterboard door in between

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: six metres with one plasterboard door your PS5 has a proper 2x2 MIMO Wi-Fi 6 radio built in which will blow those old AV600 powerline plugs out of the water

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: really i always thought wired powerline was better for gaming than wi-fi

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: a direct cat6 ethernet cable to the router beats everything but clean 5 gigahertz Wi-Fi 6 over six metres is way cleaner and faster than five-year-old powerline adapters sharing a circuit with a tumble dryer

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: fair point let's test putting the PS5 onto 5 gigahertz wi-fi right now while the tumble dryer is still running

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: let's do it first i'm going to tune your Hub 4's 5 gigahertz radio from my console here so your PS5 gets a clean uncongested channel

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: oh nice what can you tweak on the router from your end

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: i've just scanned your neighbouring flats' wi-fi and everyone around you is bunched up on channel 36 so i'm moving your 5 gigahertz band to upper channel 149 at 80 megahertz width

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: class and can you turn on QoS for gaming packets on the Hub 4 as well

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: already ahead of you padraig i have just enabled WMM QoS voice and gaming packet prioritisation on your Hub 4 and assigned UPnP port mapping for PlayStation Network

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: legend okay i've just unplugged the ethernet lead from the back of the PS5 and pulled both TP-Link plugs out of the walls

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: great now on your PS5 go to Settings then Network then Set Up Internet Connection and press the Options button on your DualSense controller over your S-Net Wi-Fi name

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: okay i'm hovering over S-Net-Hub4-992C and pressing the Options button... it pops up Wi-Fi Frequency Bands!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: change Wi-Fi Frequency Bands from Automatic to 5 GHz Only so the PlayStation never tries to drop down onto 2.4 gigahertz and then connect

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: selected 5 GHz Only... connecting to Wi-Fi network... checking internet connection... NAT Type 2 and connected!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: i can see your PS5 connected on channel 149 right now with a minus 44 dBm signal which is virtually full strength and a link rate of 866 megabits per second

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: 866 megabits! those old homeplugs were capping me at like 75 megabits! let me run the in-game network diagnostics test right now

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: fire it up padraig and tell me what ping jitter and packet loss numbers the console reports now

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: running the 60-second packet test in the game menu now... hold on it's halfway through and the graph is a completely flat green line

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: flat green is what we love to see especially with the tumble dryer still spinning in the kitchen

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: mate listen to this average latency 11 milliseconds jitter 1.2 milliseconds and 0.0 percent packet loss! down from 180 milliseconds!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: 11 milliseconds ping and zero packet loss that is night and day padraig your squad won't have any excuses left tonight

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: haha now if i miss a shot it's 100 percent on my aim and not the internet! seriously kieran you really know your stuff

transcript.text: happy to help a fellow gamer out mate i've also saved a static DHCP lease for your PS5 on the Hub 4 so your NAT Type 2 and QoS rules stay locked onto it permanently

transcript.text: and what DNS servers should i leave set on the PlayStation network settings

transcript.text: you can leave primary DNS on the Hub 4 gateway as it caches low-latency local CDN lookups for PlayStation Network updates

transcript.text: sweet i'll leave the DNS on automatic then

transcript.text: and if you ever decide to run a flat cat6 ethernet cable along the skirting board in the future the gigabit LAN ports on the Hub 4 are ready to go

transcript.text: that is top tier service honestly if i hadn't spoken to you i'd have been blaming the fibre line for weeks

transcript.text: powerline adapters catch loads of people out when heavy kitchen appliances kick in so just to confirm is your PS5 connection completely sorted now with 11ms ping and zero packet loss

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: 100 percent sorted kieran latency is rock steady at 11 milliseconds and zero packet loss on the live test

transcript.text: awesome stuff padraig is there anything else i can check or tweak on your broadband for you tonight

transcript.text: nothing at all mate i'm jumping straight back into my lobby now thanks a million
